findings.quote:
for browser in test_class.browsers[1:]:
                browser_test_class = cls.__new__(
                    cls,
                    "%s%s" % (capfirst(browser), name),
                    (test_class,),
findings.explanation: This lexical call capitalizes each additional browser name before prefixing it to the original test-class name. At runtime it is reached only for a non-browser-specific class containing tests and having a nonempty browsers list; it runs once per browser after the first. The earlier return for browser-specific or test-free classes, an empty list, or a one-browser list prevents execution.

All three lexical calls execute when this method constructs its ValidationError: they capitalize the model verbose name, the constrained field's verbose name, and the date field's verbose name. There is no conditional or early return inside this caller.

There are three lexical call sites. The model verbose name is always capitalized first. A one-field check then capitalizes that field's verbose name and returns immediately; otherwise the comprehension's single source-level call capitalizes every participating field label at runtime before the composite-error return.

The call capitalizes the model field's verbose name to create the form field's default label. It executes unconditionally while building defaults, even when a later label keyword overrides that default; there is no preceding early return.

When the foreign key is not itself the formset's primary-key field, this call capitalizes the foreign key's verbose name as a fallback error-message label. Because Python evaluates getattr() arguments eagerly, the call runs on that branch even if the existing form field has a label. The primary-key-equals-foreign-key branch skips it.

This nested function—not get_deleted_objects itself—is the lexical caller. Its first call always capitalizes the object's model verbose name whenever the callback runs, producing the no-link label. The second capitalizes the same label again only for a registered model whose change URL resolves; an unregistered model or the NoReverseMatch early return uses the first result. At runtime the callback is only created after the outer function's empty-input early return and is invoked later by the collector or protected-object iteration.

If short_description is available, the early return avoids the call. On AttributeError, the fallback replaces underscores in the action name with spaces, capitalizes its first character, and returns that description.

This caller has four lexical call sites. With year, month, and day selected, it capitalizes a YEAR_MONTH_FORMAT back-link title and a MONTH_DAY_FORMAT choice title, then returns. With year and month selected, the comprehension capitalizes each day's MONTH_DAY_FORMAT title. With only a year selected, the later month comprehension capitalizes each month's YEAR_MONTH_FORMAT title. The no-lookup/year-list branch has no call, and cl.date_hierarchy being false bypasses all four; each selected branch returns immediately.

findings.explanation: The call capitalizes the configured user model's username-field verbose name and installs it as the form label only when the field currently has no label. An existing label skips the call.

The call capitalizes the username field's verbose name in the immediate 'cannot be blank' CommandError. It is reachable only in interactive mode, after the non-TTY check, when username is exactly the empty string. Truthy usernames take the validation branch, None proceeds to prompting, and noninteractive execution skips this site.

The call always capitalizes the prompted field's verbose name at the start of the input prompt. The default-value and remote-relation suffixes are conditional, but neither condition controls this call and there is no earlier return.

The call capitalizes the username field's verbose name only when username is falsy, producing the blank-value error. If uniqueness checking finds an existing user, the earlier 'already taken' return prevents it; nonblank values proceed to field cleaning without executing this call.
